page: Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz and includes a 50 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It also includes 524 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% category. Similarly, single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are weak. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 13143.0 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6785.0. Memory bandwidth is solid, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 733.16 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 44.06 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the E32-16s_v3 is its moderate CPU compute capability paired with a massive memory footprint. While single-threaded processing is slow, the high resource density of 256 GB of RAM makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy tasks. It delivers average performance in database operations with a PassMark database score of 5386.69 and Redis SET operations reaching 12.39 million operations per second, indicating strong efficiency for in-memory data structures.

Given these characteristics, this server is best suited for memory-intensive applications. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data buffering, and enterprise applications requiring high RAM capacity without needing top-tier single-core CPU speeds.
